 versus
 Roop Chand & Ors.

Coram:
 Hon'Ble Ms. Justice Tara Vitasta Ganju
 Order

The present Appeal has been filed on behalf of the Appellant under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 17.08.2013 [hereinafter referred to as "Impugned Award"] passed by learned Presiding Officer, MACT-II, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi.
By the Impugned Award, compensation in the sum of Rs. 13.46 lakhs has been awarded to the Respondents/Claimants along with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum.

2. A Coordinate Bench of this Court by an Order dated 25.10.2013 had passed directions for stay of proceedings subject to the Appellant/Insurance Company depositing 80% of the awarded amount along with up to date interest.
The Court had further directed that the deposited amounts shall be released to the Respondent Nos. 1 to 3/Claimants.
3. The report of the Registry is that the Respondent Nos. 4 and 5 remain unserved while the service report of the Respondent Nos. 1 to 3 is awaited.
4. Learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the Appellant submits that This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 08/08/2025 at 23:46:26 she limits her challenge in the present Appeal to two grounds.
Firstly, to the grant of multiplier of 18, which, as per learned Counsel, has been wrongfully computed in this case.
She submits that the deceased was a bachelor at the time of the accident and the multiplier should have been applied on the age of the parents.
Secondly, to the deduction which has been granted at the rate of 50%.

It is submitted that the deduction should have been at the rate 40% in terms of the judgments of the Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi and Ors.; (2017) 16 SCC 680 Sarla Verma & Ors. v. DTC & Anr; ( 2009) 6 SCC 121.
